name: Advanced Performance Profiling Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for performance profiling intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for performance profiling intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When performance profiling decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Keep performance profiling changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Document any non-obvious performance profiling decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to performance profiling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. When multiple performance profiling strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Before starting performance profiling work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Keep performance profiling outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Validate performance profiling outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. Prefer explicit, readable performance profiling solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Check that performance profiling terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of performance profiling correctness.
- Do not silently drop performance profiling edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic performance profiling advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new performance profiling abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for performance profiling, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
